title: Fluidic Shaping over arbitrary domains: theory and high order finite-elements solver
summary: Fluidic Shaping is a novel method for fabrication of optical components based on the equilibrium state of liquid volumes in neutral buoyancy, subjected to geometrical constraints. The underlying physics of this method is described by a highly nonlinear partial differential equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions and an integral constraint. To date, useful solutions for such optical liquid surfaces could be obtained analytically only for the linearized equations and only on circular or elliptical domains.
